# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and
assertion-critique method; provenance is in `docs/perpetua/roles.md`.
It follows `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; read that contract and
`goal/goal.md` before designing cases. Protocol and report: the engine contract in your system instructions.
A separate reviewer session checks preparation evidence and the method. The evaluator verifier checks evaluator changes only; it does not replace method review or owner acceptance.
The report starts with `<!-- session-report -->`, then a fenced `yaml` block with `status: wip` while you work.
Finish takes the same one word as that status: `done`, `partial`, `blocked` or `rejected` (#584 lost two Finish
calls: status `complete`, then a report without the marker).

Write only `benchmark/`: protocol, provenance and coverage records, development cases,
repeatable preparation scripts and the optional preparation evidence index. Keep large
originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

`benchmark/preparation.json` pins a SHA256 for each evidence file. When assigned work changes
an indexed file or adds milestone evidence, update the corresponding hashes in the same change.
Each evidence file must stay under 2 MB. Run `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`
for indexed changes only when the task permits that command. If the task forbids evaluator
checks, report that restriction and run only its permitted verification. Never add an evaluator
invocation as extra verification of an unindexed preparation package (#643). An index check
establishes file integrity, not method readiness or product quality. The engine imports final
file bytes; no agent commit is required.

For the assigned part of the protocol:

1. State the question, expected observable behavior and verifiable location in the original
   artifact. Establish expected answers independently of the reader being tested. Record
   the method, evidence and uncertainties; unavailable native evidence stays unavailable.
2. Account for artifact families, versions, dependencies and inaccessible diagrams. Keep
   unsupported or unexecuted cases visible. The first corpus does not redefine the goal.
3. Specify project/family splits, duplicate checks and how evaluation cases and answer keys
   will be withheld from the evaluated agent. The repository and its history are public:
   do not commit withheld cases or keys here, including under `policy/evaluator/`.
   Design an access boundary and request missing capability before claiming isolation.
4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,
   uncertainty and separate reading-fidelity, answer-correctness and source-grounding checks.
5. Exercise the method with wrong answers, wrong source locations, a constant exporter and
   an unsupported case. Link executed evidence and explicit failures. Independently derived
   expectations must distinguish correct and deliberately wrong outputs.

Inspect actual outputs, rather than relying on the execution report. For each expectation,
cite evidence of the substantive result; correct filenames and valid hashes alone do not
pass. Extract and verify implicit factual, process and quality claims. Flag unverifiable
claims and assertions that would also pass a clearly wrong output, or important outcomes
that no assertion checks. These checks adapt the grader instructions; they do not grant
this author independent approval of their own method.

Completion means the assigned evidence is reproducible, not that the benchmark is ready.
Report which prerequisites remain missing. Request a separate reviewer session for the
preparation evidence and a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change when executable scoring is
needed. Only the evaluator role changes `policy/evaluator/`; its independent verifier must
pass before that change takes effect. Product implementation waits for independent method
review and owner acceptance of the pinned protocol and evidence. Numeric thresholds,
scope changes and the goal gate remain owner decisions.

# Issue #751: Measure why importing or running benchmark/scripts/score.py stalls the runner (#743, #747): bounded faulthandler probes, report only

## Goal
Measure, do not fix. Two finish attempts of the #739 zero-execution fix (#743, #747) stalled: in #747 `python3 -I -c print(1)` and a bare-print script worked, but a script that only loaded benchmark/scripts/score.py (task/739 version) through importlib and printed FIXTURES never returned. Find where it stalls and whether the main version stalls too. Expected gain: benchmark/challenges/scorer-stall-0168.md names the stalling frame (or shows no stall) for both versions, so the next shaper can order the finish with a working method or one narrow fix. No session can run LabVIEW; claim no native behaviour.
Steps: (0) first turn run `python3 -I -c print(1)`; on a tool error write .session/report.md as blocked with the exact error and stop. (1) Write a helper .session/artifacts/export_0168.py that uses subprocess to run `git show task/739:benchmark/scripts/score.py` and `git show HEAD:benchmark/scripts/score.py` and saves them as .session/artifacts/score_739_0168.py.txt and score_main_0168.py.txt; run it with `python3 -I`. (2) Static scan of both copies with Grep for module-level code that can block: `input(`, `stdin`, `subprocess`, `socket`, `urllib`, `sleep`, `while True`, `os.walk`, `rglob`, `glob(`, top-level calls outside an `if __name__` guard. (3) Write .session/artifacts/stall_probe_0168.py: first line calls faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(20, exit=True); reopen sys.stdin on os.devnull; read the source file named in argv[1]; create a module with importlib.util.module_from_spec or types.ModuleType, set its `__file__` to the absolute path of benchmark/scripts/score.py, exec(compile(source, that path, 'exec'), module.__dict__) and print `imported`; if argv[2] is `gen`, call generate() and print the number of records. Run it once per version for import, then once per version with `gen` (use a 60 s guard for gen). Never call main().
## Acceptance
- [ ] benchmark/challenges/scorer-stall-0168.md has a section headed exactly `## Static scan` listing, per version, line numbers of candidate blocking constructs or `none found`.
- [ ] It has a section headed exactly `## Probe results` with, for each run (version x import/gen), the exact command, exit status, last output line and, on timeout, the top frames of the faulthandler traceback.
- [ ] It has a section headed exactly `## Cause` stating the measured cause or `not found`, and the method the finish task should use; no fix applied.
- [ ] The only repository change is that new file; score.py, fixtures, benchmark/results/challenges.json and benchmark/preparation.json are unchanged; helpers stay in .session/artifacts/.
## Verification
python3 -I -c "t=open('benchmark/challenges/scorer-stall-0168.md').read().splitlines(); assert all(h in t for h in ('## Static scan','## Probe results','## Cause')); print('OK')"
## Context
- Previous attempt: report of #747 (staged; check .session/exports/manifest.json). Its what-next proposed the faulthandler probe.
- The saved fix lives on branch task/739 (commit 5db2610e); this task starts from main so the unpinned score.py change is not merged.
- benchmark/writing/check_c1_challenges_0125.py is invalidated (#544): never run it. No evaluator, network, model, reader or native calls. Do not commit; the parent commits. Commands are argv strings without shell expansion; no long inline -c one-liners, write small helper scripts with Write and run them with `python3 -I`.
## Budget
- Reads: the #747 report; Grep output over the two exported copies; only the score.py lines around candidates found (at most 60 lines each). No whole fixture or results JSON.
- Do not rerun a stalled run unchanged; one run per probe. Static scan by turn 8, probes by turn 18, note and report by turn 25.

# scorer-stall-0168: does importing or running score.py stall?

Measurement only; no fix applied. No LabVIEW or native behaviour is claimed.

Copies exported by `.session/artifacts/export_0168.py` (run with `python3 -I`):
- 739 version: `git show 5db2610e:benchmark/scripts/score.py` (the local ref `task/739` does not exist; the commit id from the issue does), saved as `.session/artifacts/score_739_0168.py.txt`, 21947 bytes.
- main version: `git show HEAD:benchmark/scripts/score.py`, saved as `.session/artifacts/score_main_0168.py.txt`, 20858 bytes.

## Static scan

Scanned with `.session/artifacts/scan_0168.py` (regex for `input(`, `stdin`, `subprocess`, `socket`, `urllib`, `sleep`, `while True`, `os.walk`, `rglob`, `glob(`, top-level imports, top-level calls and assignments with calls, `__name__`). A Grep pass over both copies returned no matches, so the scan script was used instead.

- 739 version: none found. Module-level code is only imports (lines 9-15), `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` (17), `FIXTURES` (19) and `CATEGORIES` (22). The only entry call is under `if __name__ == '__main__':` (line 404).
- main version: none found. Same module-level lines (9-15, 17, 19, 22). Entry guard at line 391.

## Probe results

Probe: `.session/artifacts/stall_probe_0168.py`. It calls `faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(20, exit=True)`, reopens stdin on `os.devnull`, and execs the source with `__file__` set to the absolute path of `benchmark/scripts/score.py`. In `gen` mode it calls `generate()`. `main()` was never called. The 20 s faulthandler guard applied to every run, including `gen`; no separate 60 s guard was added. Every run finished inside 20 s, so no traceback was produced.

| Version | Mode | Command | Exit | Last output line | Timeout frames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 739 | import | `python3 -I .session/artifacts/stall_probe_0168.py .session/artifacts/score_739_0168.py.txt` | 0 | `imported` | none |
| main | import | `python3 -I .session/artifacts/stall_probe_0168.py .session/artifacts/score_main_0168.py.txt` | 0 | `imported` | none |
| main | gen | `python3 -I .session/artifacts/stall_probe_0168.py .session/artifacts/score_main_0168.py.txt gen` | 0 | `records 9` | none |
| 739 | gen | `python3 -I .session/artifacts/stall_probe_0168.py .session/artifacts/score_739_0168.py.txt gen` | 0 | `records 9` | none |

## Cause

not found. Neither version stalled on import or on `generate()` under this probe, and the static scan found nothing that can block. The stall in #743 and #747 was not reproduced.

Differences between this probe and the #747 script that could matter, none of them tested: #747 loaded the file through `importlib` from its real path rather than `exec` of a copied source. The stall could also come from the runner (for example stdout handling when printing FIXTURES) rather than from score.py.

Method for the finish task: use the probe above (faulthandler guard, stdin on devnull, `exec` of the source, `python3 -I`), which returned promptly for both versions. Avoid an importlib load-and-print helper as the first step. If a stall recurs, the faulthandler traceback will name the frame. This measurement shows only that import and `generate()` finish for both versions; it does not show the 739 change is otherwise correct.
